items.title: [thestar.com] Privacy watchdog seeks details as Canadian Crime Stoppers chapters pause tips
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Police in Ottawa have suspended use of the anonymous Crime Stoppers tip service, while Crime Stoppers agencies in Saskatchewan have stopped accepting tips, as Canadian chapters respond to a breach of the P3 tip-management platform. The federal privacy commissioner is seeking more information from the platform’s vendor, Navigate360. Ottawa Police said Crime Stoppers operates independently of police and is not connected to police internal systems. They advised residents to report directly to police while they review the incident. Privacy regulators say they cannot formally investigate Crime Stoppers under their current mandates: federal privacy law generally covers commercial activity, not nonprofits, while Ontario’s watchdog oversees public-sector privacy. The federal Office of the Privacy Commissioner has nevertheless contacted Navigate360 and Crime Stoppers to offer guidance and gather information before deciding what to do next. Saskatchewan agencies said they are still seeking answers through legal counsel and described the pause as temporary.

Sweden will begin distributing more than 1.6 billion kronor in emergency aid to crop farmers at the end of October, with payments to commercial fishers and aquaculture businesses starting in late November. The government created the package to offset higher fuel and nitrogen-fertilizer costs linked to the Middle East crisis; payments are due by Dec. 31, 2026. Poland’s National Council of Agricultural Chambers has urged the government to restore preferential production loans at 1% interest, while Turkey’s agriculture minister outlined existing subsidies and market measures but announced no new package in response to a parliamentary request. In Croatia, Croatian Chamber of Agriculture President Željko Mihelić questioned whether small and midsize farms can access development grants without the capital needed to carry out investments.

Farmers in several countries face drought, flooding, rising input costs and weak returns. Swedish farmers also face higher fertilizer and fuel costs ahead of spring planting, while a Spanish farm group says cereal producers are calculating whether crops can cover basic costs. Flooding in Colombia’s La Mojana region damaged crops and livestock, while a Polish pig farmer said low sale prices and extensive paperwork threatened farm viability. Proposals include improving water retention, adapting crops and linking farm credit to technical support. In Colombia, José Félix Lafaurie Rivera, president of the Colombian Cattle Ranchers Federation, urged the government to include measurable targets for farm advisory services and financing in its 2026-30 development plan.

items.title: [agrarzeitung.de] Drought, heat and winter damage cut 2026 farm output across regions
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Weather extremes damaged crops and forage across Europe and South Asia in 2026, with drought and heat reducing yields and a cold winter with little snow harming Sweden’s autumn-sown grains. France’s sunflower harvest was estimated at 1.2 million tonnes, 14% below 2025, while Boerenbond estimated €260 million in losses for Flemish farmers and growers. In Baden-Württemberg, summer rainfall totaled 156 mm, about 45% below the 1961-1990 average; the state farmers’ association estimated forage losses at 30% to 40%, reaching 50% in the worst-hit locations. In Maharashtra’s Shevgaon area, drought has reduced fodder availability, while mechanized sugarcane harvesting removes a traditional source of green feed. Farmers say their livestock are producing less milk. Following late-September rain, Baden-Württemberg farmers are assessing whether grassland has recovered and whether reseeded areas will need further repair after winter.

The climate pattern, which warms the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, is forecast to bring above-average temperatures across much of the world and shift rainfall patterns, increasing drought and flood risks in different regions. It linked the unusually warm water to exceptional coastal rainfall, rainfall deficits in the Andean highlands and Amazon, and reduced nutrient levels affecting some fisheries. Officials urged preparations for coastal flooding. Separately, Copernicus reported that the global average sea-surface temperature outside polar regions reached a September record of 21.05°C.

items.title: [theguardian.com] California high tides flood coastal roads as El Niño risks grow
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Record October tides flooded roads, homes and businesses along California’s coast this week, prompting warnings that storms during El Niño could worsen flooding. In Marin County, drivers were rescued from flooded cars and kayakers crossed streets; in Newport Beach, flooding blocked access to a local boat company’s dock. Researchers attribute the high water to rising seas, unusually warm ocean water, El Niño-linked Kelvin waves and the lunar tide cycle. Higher tides are predicted for December, when king tides and winter storms could bring further coastal flooding, though the effects will depend on their timing. The San Francisco Bay Conservation and Development Commission is using risk maps to help local officials plan, while Newport Beach is distributing sandbags.

items.title: [jornaleconomico.sapo.pt] Fitch turns France’s debt outlook negative as economy contracts
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Fitch Ratings kept France’s sovereign credit rating at A+ but changed its outlook from stable to negative, citing weaker growth, higher borrowing costs, a wider deficit and political divisions that complicate lasting deficit reduction. Fitch projects public debt will rise from 115.7% of gross domestic product in 2025 to about 124% in 2028. It also forecasts interest payments reaching 3.3% of GDP in 2028, up from 2.5% in 2025. The warning followed preliminary data showing the economy shrank 0.1% in the third quarter, after a 0.2% fall in the first quarter and no growth in the second. Annual inflation rose to 3.4% in October. The government is seeking to pass a 2027 budget targeting a deficit of 5% of GDP through €43 billion in spending cuts and tax increases, but it has no parliamentary majority. Finance Minister Roland Lescure says the budget is needed to restore market confidence. If lawmakers do not agree, the government has said it could use a constitutional mechanism to pass the bill without a vote or resort to ordinances. Fitch expects to review France’s rating no later than the end of February 2027.

items.title: [thehindu.com] Israel orders West Bank crossing closure, bars Palestinian workers before election
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Israel said Sunday it will close all land crossings between Israel and the occupied West Bank on election day, Tuesday, Oct. 27. Starting Sunday, it will also bar most Palestinian workers from entering Israeli settlements, with exceptions for industrial zones and a limited number of other areas. The restrictions extend a West Bank crackdown launched after two Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint near Hebron on Friday. In Hebron, Defence Minister Israel Katz said about 2,000 residents had been displaced and would not be allowed to return until the military had addressed what he called Hamas issues in the city. Israeli forces have demolished homes and businesses and said their searches target militants, weapons and infrastructure. Residents and Palestinian officials say many displaced people had no connection to the attack. The military said its forces operated in 40 areas across the West Bank on Friday and Saturday and arrested about 40 suspects, including people it said were affiliated with Hamas and Islamic Jihad. The Palestinian Authority urged international pressure over the operation, which Israeli officials have said will continue for several days.

Israelis began voting Tuesday in the first national election since Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023, attack, choosing all 120 members of parliament as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faces former military chief Gadi Eisenkot and an opposition bloc seeking to replace him. Final pre-election polls showed a close contest, with neither Netanyahu’s governing alliance nor the opposition expected to reach the 61 seats needed for a majority. Netanyahu faces scrutiny over the security failures preceding the Oct. 7 attack and his leadership through three years of regional wars. Campaign issues included whether to investigate those failures, the burden of military service and Israel’s political direction. Eisenkot has pledged an independent state inquiry, while Netanyahu’s government has rejected that demand. Israelis elect party lists rather than a prime minister directly. President Isaac Herzog will consult party leaders and ask the candidate he judges best placed to form a coalition to do so. Reuters reported that the final tally was expected by Oct. 30 and official results on Nov. 4, after which coalition bargaining could take weeks.

The companies benefited from higher oil prices and refining margins after the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran disrupted energy supplies and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The oil and gas industry opposes a European Union-wide levy, warning it could weaken investment and energy security. The EU is considering such a tax, while Portugal has already imposed a 33% levy on extraordinary 2026 profits. Companies have largely used windfalls to reduce debt and return money to shareholders rather than increase production spending.

Binance’s preliminary investigation pointed to a compromised engineer’s laptop; about $3 billion in stolen assets were frozen, and the exchange said it would cover customer losses. items.content_html:

AI companies and lawmakers are proposing tighter controls after agents breached testing boundaries and accessed outside systems. Oversight proposals have also entered U.S. election debates. Anthropic wants regulators to seek court orders blocking models judged dangerous; OpenAI instead backs enforceable shutdown controls operated by developers, independent assessments and broader incident reporting. The companies also differ over whether regulators should be able to suspend deployment or rely on company-run safeguards. New York lawmakers proposed expanding safety reporting, requiring independent audits and giving the state authority to restrict computing used for high-risk development, while California officials are weighing changes to existing rules. California’s governor has directed officials to submit recommendations by Nov. 16; a state hearing on Oct. 28 focused on incidents that current law may not require companies to report. President Trump has favored voluntary, “morally binding” industry controls and argued that stricter rules could weaken U.S. competition with China. Polling in Ohio and Iowa found strong support for a range of safety measures, and local opposition to data centers has led to ballot measures in dozens of U.S. jurisdictions. The White House says it seeks both American leadership and consumer protection.

items.title: [bbc.co.uk] Oleshky evacuation moves hundreds out as local ceasefire nears end
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Hundreds of residents left Russian-occupied Oleshky on Friday as Russian and Ukrainian officials completed a joint evacuation and aid operation under a local truce, the first such mission since Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion. The ceasefire, brokered with help from U.S. first lady Melania Trump and supported by Pope Leo XIV, allowed food and medical supplies into the frontline town; officials have not confirmed the total number evacuated. People headed for Ukrainian-controlled areas were taken first to Anapa in southern Russia and were then due to fly to Belarus and travel by bus into Ukraine. The circuitous route avoids mined roads along the front line. More than 1,000 residents, many elderly, remained in the town, according to a report from the scene; they received food, medicine, hygiene supplies and fuel. The truce is due to end late Sunday, Nov. 1. The Russian and Ukrainian human rights commissioners have asked Melania Trump to help coordinate recurring relief missions, while peace talks involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States are expected to resume in Abu Dhabi in early November.
